body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). Agents work on a dirty tree almost all the time. Today the packet reports `mixed-worktree`, trace recording is blocked in that state, `features`, `overview` and `review` require a clean tree, and the snapshot is keyed by tree OID with a full rebuild per tree (V1-0328). Cursor syncs only changed Merkle subtrees and Augment picks up working-tree changes immediately. Hashing dirty files with the Git blob formula gives synthetic blob ids that keep invariant 1 pinning, while the overlay reuses the committed snapshot without a daemon.
